mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months but S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS on 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 8.0% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that triggers a flight to quality in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 8.0% and remains above 8.0% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 8.0% for two consecutive months but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for UNRATE on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate earnings growth expectations decline, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both decline for two consecutive months but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (HOUST and RSAFS) on 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing slowdowns (INDPRO < 100 for two consecutive months), the signal of weakening industrial activity triggers a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 for two consecutive months but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for INDPRO on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually compresses real equity returns by increasing the real risk-free rate, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5% annually but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) falls below 50,000 jobs, it signals a slowing labor market that reduces consumer spending confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth < 50,000 but S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for PAYEMS growth on 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad economic slowdown, which triggers a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 and INDPRO both decline for two consecutive periods but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term (GDPC1 and INDPRO) on 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and rising), the central bank's policy shift increases the cost of capital, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and rising but S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC for FEDFUNDS on 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
